chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from some of his companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

He asked: 'What is the distance between you and the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' I replied: 'Sixteen parasangs.' He asked: 'Do you not go to him?' I replied: 'No.' He said: 'How negligent you people are!'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the negligence of those who do not visit the grave of Imam al-Husayn?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) highlights the physical proximity of the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.)—only sixteen parasangs away—to underscore the spiritual distance caused by the companions' neglect. The term 'jafā' (negligence/aloofness) serves as a critique of their failure to maintain the bond of love and visitation (ziyarah) with the Ahl al-Bayt, a central tenet of Shia piety in Shia tradition. This narration emphasizes that physical closeness does not excuse spiritual remoteness, urging believers to actively seek out the shrines of the Imams.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 1. My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from ‘Ali ibn Ḥakam, from some of his companions, who said: Abū Ja’far (Imam Bāqir (a.s.))

asked, “What is the distance between you and the grave of Ḥusain?” I replied, “Sixteen parasangs.” Imam (a.s.) asked, “Do you not go to him?” I replied, “No.” Imam (a.s.) said, “How negligent you people are!!!”
